text: Good API design makes applications easier to build and maintain. When creating REST APIs, developers should use clear and meaningful endpoints that represent resources, such as /users or /orders. Each endpoint should return the correct HTTP status codes, like 200 for success, 404 when something is not found, and 500 for server errors. Clear documentation is also essential, because it helps other developers understand how to use the API without confusion. Finally, versioning is important: by including a version number in the URL, such as /v1/users, developers can update the API without breaking existing applications. Following these practices leads to reliable and user-friendly APIs.
